newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia, China ministers avoid Dalai Lama issue.
newsitem.headline: Australia, China ministers avoid Dalai Lama issue.

text.p: Australian Foreign Minister Alexander Downer said on Friday he had enjoyed a glass of champagne with his Chinese counterpart and neither of them had mentioned a row over a visit to Australia by the Dalai Lama.
On Tuesday Beijing threatened possible trade retaliation against Australia when Prime Minister John Howard agreed to meet the exiled Tibetan spirtual leader.

The meeting went ahead in Sydney on Thursday and was immediately criticised by the Chinese. But Downer told Australian radio from New York that neither he nor Qian Qichen mentioned the Dalai Lama when the two men met on Thursday evening at the United Nations.

"What we don't want to do is inflame the situation and we're obviously not trying to," Downer said. "We have a simple position on this issue. We've established that position and that, as far as we're concerned, is the beginning and the end of it."
Downer met Qian to sign a formal agreement on an Australian consulate in Hong Kong after the British colony's transfer to Chinese rule in the middle of next year.
After signing the agreement, Downer said: "We enjoyed a glass of champagne."

The ministers also discussed the nuclear test ban treaty signed in New York this week. Adoption of the treaty was blocked at negotiations in Geneva but Australia -- supported by China and the other declared nuclear powers -- led a diplomatic drive to revive it at the U.N. General Assembly.
